Lighter Security Incident Update: Approximately 5M USDC Returned to Affected Trader, Withdrawals Resumed

Lighter said in its November 16 security incident report that an attacker exploited nonce reuse in unofficial signing code used by certain trading accounts to derive API private keys from public signatures. The attacker then created a public pool through a compromised account, transferred funds into the pool, and extracted assets by redeeming pool shares through an attacker-controlled account. Lighter confirmed that its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure, and official SDKs were unaffected.

The incident triggered its smart contract-based Guardian mechanism, temporarily pausing withdrawals and allowing the Security Council to return approximately 5 million USDC to the affected trader. Withdrawals have since resumed, with pending requests being processed. Lighter has implemented wallet signature requirements for public pool transfers and made API key signatures non-public. It also plans to introduce IP allowlists, per-key permissions and limits, and proactively monitor and revoke API keys at risk from nonce reuse. — link

64,000 Bitcoin Mining Machines Hijacked, Redirecting 13 EH/s to OCEAN Pool

Bitcoin News reported that approximately 64,000 Bitcoin mining machines, representing about 13 EH/s of hashrate, were hijacked around 20:00 U.S. Central Time on November 14. The attackers redirected the hashrate to OCEAN and replaced the mining payout address with one they controlled, briefly pushing the pool's hashrate close to 50 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting said the incident appeared to have ended on November 15, with the affected hashrate falling to around 100 PH/s. The attackers failed to mine any blocks and received no block rewards, although affected miners lost mining revenue during the incident. A potential compromise of Luxor Commander software has not been independently confirmed. — link

Prediction Market Regulatory Dispute Deepens as Senators Challenge CFTC and Hyperliquid Policy Center Backs Federal Oversight

Nine Democratic senators, including Adam Schiff, Amy Klobuchar and Elissa Slotkin, urged CFTC Chairman Michael Selig to halt efforts to challenge state restrictions on prediction markets, arguing that the agency's actions conflict with existing court orders and undermine state and tribal laws. The request follows a November 5 CFTC directive requiring regulated platforms to remove certain geographic restrictions within 30 days.

Meanwhile, the Hyperliquid Policy Center backed the CFTC's rulemaking, arguing that event contracts traded on registered exchanges should be regulated as federal derivatives rather than state-level gambling products. Multiple states are separately suing prediction market operators over alleged unlicensed gambling. — link
